subject: Intermittent eviction spikes during peak — coordinated action plan
content:
From: Ava Morgan <ava.morgan@appsynth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:24:12 -0700
Subject: Intermittent evictions and 429s during high-concurrency runs

Hi Ben —

We started seeing a burst of 429s and "reservation eviction" errors in the morning runs around 09:10 UTC today. The pattern looks like short (30–90s) windows where high-concurrency load (~1200 concurrent streams) causes jobs to be evicted and queued requests to fail with 429.

Key notes:
- Affected routes: /v1/stream-gen (customer-facing), several long-context requests.
- We saw increased tails on tail_latency (p99.9 ~ 7.6s) and a sharp drop in throughput during the windows.
- We captured traces and logs (attached: eviction-trace-20270411.log).

Can Redwood confirm if this maps to autoscale activity or a scheduling/eviction bug on dedicated pools? This is impacting a handful of customers and our internal QA. We can provide a replay window tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Morgan
Head of Platform | AppSynth
ava.morgan@appsynth.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 18:45:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent evictions and 429s during high-concurrency runs

Quick initial findings after a first-pass investigation:
- The dedicated GPU pool serving AppSynth entered a transient backpressure state at 09:08–09:12 UTC. We observed aggressive eviction of warm instances when host-level memory oversubscription exceeded the safety threshold (configured headroom = 12%).
- Autoscaler triggered a small reclaim cycle at 09:09 UTC that appears to have raced with inflight allocations, producing queue buildup and 429s. The reclaim decision was driven by a spike in cross-tenant memory reservations from a different reserved customer (multi-tenant burst).

Short-term mitigations applied (11 Apr):
- Increased headroom to 18% for the AppSynth pool (temporary).
- Flipped fallback routing to the reserved burst pool (cold warm-standby) for high-latency requests — this reduced observed 429s in our internal replay.
- Uploaded a snapshot of the runbook we used (runbook-snapshot.png) and logs (eviction-trace-20270411.log).

Next steps (owners):
- Karthik: tune autoscale hysteresis to avoid aggressive reclaim on <30s spikes (owner: karthik_iyer).
- Infra: consider moving AppSynth to an isolated reserved lane if they want guaranteed headroom (owner: ben_carter for customer conversation).
- Ops: schedule a canary replay tomorrow 09:00–10:00 UTC to verify mitigations (owner: irene_choi).

I'll prepare a short customer-facing note and an ops playbook we can attach.

Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer

---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morgan <ava.morgan@appsynth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, procurement@appsynth.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:05 -0700
Subject: Action plan: short-term mitigations + canary window (details and attachments)

Hi Ava —

Thank you for the quick report and the logs. We reproduced the pattern in our replay and implemented the following immediate mitigations (already active):
- Raised pool safety headroom to 18% for AppSynth traffic (temporary change).
- Enabled reserved-burst fallback for the most latency-sensitive route (/v1/stream-gen).
- Queued a canary replay for 09:00–09:30 UTC tomorrow to validate the fix under controlled load.

Attachments: ops_playbook_v1.pdf (short ops checklist), eviction-trace-20270411.log, runbook-snapshot.png

What to expect:
- We expect a meaningful reduction in 429s during the mitigation window, though throughput may be slightly reduced while headroom is increased.
- If the canary looks good, we’ll keep mitigations in place and schedule a follow-up discussion to review permanent options (dedicated isolated lane, autoscaler tuning, slow-start warm pooling).

Compensation: Given the impact, I’ve opened a credit case with our billing team and looped in procurement in case you want to discuss a longer-term reserved capacity agreement for guaranteed headroom.

Can you confirm the canary window works for you? If you prefer a different time, we can accommodate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morgan <ava.morgan@appsynth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, procurement@appsynth.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next steps: post-incident plan and RCA owners

Ava — thanks again for running the canary with us. Summary & next steps: 

What happened (brief): a transient cross-tenant memory reservation spike caused the autoscaler to reclaim capacity during a high-concurrency window. The reclaim overlapped with inflight allocations and produced short eviction bursts and 429s.

Immediate outcomes:
- Canary 09:00–09:30 UTC (12 Apr) showed 95% reduction in 429s on the targeted route; latency p95 returned to baseline.
- Temporary headroom and fallback routing remain in place pending a permanent fix.

Permanent remediation plan (owners & timeline):
- Autoscaler hysteresis and reclaim policy change (owner: karthik_iyer) — target: 3 weeks for staged rollout.
- Scheduler change: prefer soft eviction + early throttling over hard reclaim for <60s spikes (owner: marissa_cole) — target: 4 weeks.
- Offer: commercial reserved-lane proposal for guaranteed headroom and 99.9% eviction-free windows (owner: ben_carter + procurement) — propose draft by EOD Fri.

Proposed next customer touch: joint postmortem call (30–45m) to review RCA and contract options. Please share availability for Wed/Thu next week.

Attachments: ops_playbook_v1.pdf (same), and a short timeline we will share in the call.

If you’d like, I can include our engineering notes and the scheduled rollout plan in the postmortem doc.

Ben
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
